notes: Community adapter: flags verified against official OpenCode docs (2026-11-14), but OpenCode ships TWO incompatible lines under one command name - OpenCode 1 (npm package opencode-ai) and OpenCode 2 - which are not installed side by side by default. This adapter uses only the surface both lines share: `opencode run` with the prompt as the positional argument (stdin prompt delivery is not documented for run, so the prompt goes as a single quoted argument), --model in provider/model form, --agent, and --auto. Check the cliVersion recorded in the health file to learn which line you have, and confirm flags with `opencode run --help` on your install. The mode mapping is approximate: OpenCode has no native three-tier mode scale and its default permissions are permissive (most tools run without asking). There is deliberately NO readonly tier in this adapter: the plan agent denies file edits except plan files (.opencode/plans/ or ~/.opencode/plan) but does NOT restrict shell commands, and a bridge tier labeled readonly that can run arbitrary shell would break SessionBridge's readonly contract - so readonly jobs are rejected for this adapter until a bundled deny-rules profile can make the tier honest. That also means readonly jobs cannot run on OpenCode: a job for this adapter must declare accept-edits or auto explicitly, and your mode ceiling must allow it (the shipped example ceiling is readonly, so raise or remove it deliberately). accept-edits uses --agent build (the default agent, all tools enabled). auto adds --auto, which auto-approves every permission request that is not explicitly denied; deny rules still hold. There is no OS sandbox at any tier; tighten behavior with deny rules in your OpenCode permission config. The hidden aliases --dangerously-skip-permissions and --yolo are never emitted; only the documented --auto is used. Effort/variant is intentionally NOT mapped: V1 takes a separate --variant flag while V2 appends #variant to the model reference, and the runner's model pattern rejects '#'; V1 users can copy this adapter and add effortArgs ['--variant','{value}']. authCheck is null: `opencode auth list` lists stored credentials, but many installs authenticate via provider environment variables instead, and the command's exit code when signed out is not documented - there is no reliable non-interactive signed-in probe, so preflight is skipped for this adapter (same treatment as aider and gemini-cli). Config surface: opencode.json (permission rules, MCP servers) in the job's cwd applies to bridge jobs and is NOT bounded by the job's mode - see SECURITY.md.
